heading: A substantial share of sparse autoencoder (SAE) error is linearly predictable from input activations
definition: a large share of the SAE error vector is a linear function of the input activation.
summary: One independent preprint reproduced the finding using broad-domain and medical-domain SAEs on Gemma-2-9b. Evidence covers models with 1–10 billion parameters; the replication estimates were read from figure color scales, with no reported controls or uncertainty.

suggested_status.by_scale: R2 at 1-10B; ? at toy, <1B, 10-100B and >100B because those scales have no linked V1 coverage.
suggested_status.reason: The original reports substantial linear error-vector predictability, and arXiv:2508.09363 reproduces it on Gemma-2-9b layer 20 with broad-domain and medical-domain SAEs (arXiv:2410.14670#r1; arXiv:2508.09363#R1; arXiv:2508.09363#R2). counts: versions.V1.verdicts.supports.studies = 1; versions.V1.tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original = 0; versions.V1.studies_by_size contains only 1-10B. The independent evidence is a preprint with colourbar-derived ranges and no reported code, controls or uncertainty.
suggested_status.open_questions: A direct replication on a named non-Gemma family, other model scales and explicitly identified training stages would establish broader scope. Matched configuration-level results with uncertainty would clarify how predictability depends on domain, width and sparsity; an absent or reversed result under comparable conditions would change the status.

source.title: Decomposing The Dark Matter of Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Joshua Engels; L. Smith; Max Tegmark

original_result.setup: The original study fitted linear transformations from input activations to SAE error vectors across TopK and JumpReLU SAE configurations.
original_result.result: Linear predictions explained 15%–72% of the variance in SAE error vectors (R²) across the tested configurations.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: Linear prediction explained substantial error variance in GemmaScope and medical-domain SAEs.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

untested.what: Whether substantial linear predictability holds at toy, <1B, 10–100B and >100B scales.
untested.basis: counts: versions.V1.studies_by_size contains only 1-10B. The original aggregate row and the Gemma-2-9b rows provide no linked evidence at the other scales: arXiv:2410.14670#r1; arXiv:2508.09363#R1; arXiv:2508.09363#R2.

untested.what: Whether the result differs between base, instruct/chat and fine-tuned models.
untested.basis: counts: versions.V1.studies_by_stage and versions.V1.coverage_by_operation contain only stage 'not stated'. The linked rows do not establish a comparison between training stages: arXiv:2410.14670#r1; arXiv:2508.09363#R1; arXiv:2508.09363#R2.

untested.what: Independent reproduction on an explicitly identified model family other than Gemma.
untested.basis: counts: versions.V1.studies_by_family contains Gemma and 'other or not stated'. The original's aggregate model label is incomplete, while the independent study names Gemma-2-9b: arXiv:2410.14670#r1; arXiv:2508.09363#R1; arXiv:2508.09363#R2. This does not establish that the original tested no other family.

wording_issues.issue: The original reports error-vector R² ranging from 15% to 72%, whereas the independent study reports approximately 0.56–0.73 and 0.57–0.84 as R² fractions. The statement leaves the threshold for 'large' unspecified and obscures variation across settings.

The reported evidence concerns variance explained by fitted linear predictors. It supports an approximately linearly predictable component of the error vector, without establishing an exact linear decomposition or the identity of the underlying features.

method_sensitivity.what: For Gemma-2-9b layer 20, the verdict describes lower error-vector linear predictability for medical-domain JumpReLU SAEs than for broad-domain GemmaScope SAEs. The colourbar ranges are approximately 0.56–0.73 and 0.57–0.84, respectively, in R² fractions; they do not supply matched numerical comparisons for individual configurations.

The original's method-sensitivity header states that error-vector predictability varies with SAE width and L0. Its linked aggregate row reports R² of 15% to 72%, without resolving that range by individual configuration.
